Stochastic 5: Malliavin Calculus¶

Ordinary calculus differentiates with respect to a number. Malliavin calculus differentiates with respect to the noise itself: how much does a random quantity F change if the Brownian increment in one step is nudged? The answer is a number per increment, and it unlocks things the pathwise derivative cannot do. After this chapter you can compute the discrete Malliavin derivative of any functional of a path, integrate an anticipating process with the Skorokhod integral, and price a sensitivity of a payoff that has a jump in it.

The mental model¶

Discretize a Wiener path into increments ΔW_1, …, ΔW_n. A functional F of the path is a function of those increments, and the Malliavin derivative is its gradient with respect to them: D_i F = ∂F / ∂(ΔW_i). The library computes it by autodiff in one reverse pass, whatever n is. For F = W_T² it is 2 W_T on every increment; for F = max(W) it is 1 on the increments up to the position of the maximum and 0 after it.

The Skorokhod integral extends the Ito integral to processes u that may look into the future:

δ(u) = Σ u_i ΔW_i − Σ (∂u_i / ∂ΔW_i) Δt

For an adapted u the second sum vanishes and δ(u) is the Ito sum. The two are linked by the duality E[F δ(u)] = E[Σ u_i D_i F Δt], which is what makes the Malliavin derivative useful for estimating derivatives of expectations: integrating by parts moves the derivative from the payoff onto a weight.

What to remember¶

  • D_i F = ∂F/∂ΔW_i is the gradient of a functional with respect to the Brownian increments; it costs one reverse pass.

  • The Skorokhod integral is the Ito sum for adapted integrands and still defined for anticipating ones.

  • Use pathwise derivatives for smooth payoffs and a Malliavin weight for payoffs with jumps. The weight must be derived for the model and the sensitivity at hand; the library provides the derivative and the integral that make that derivation checkable.
